correctness.rationale: Primitive divisors at distinct Fibonacci indices provide distinct primes with known ranks of apparition. Lengyel's valuation formula allows their exponent parities to be independently made odd in a common Kishi index, while 5 also occurs to odd exponent. Gauss genus theory then gives the stated 2-rank bound. A Fibonacci gcd argument plus valuation stability reduces any hypothetical finite-field repetition to a fixed squarefree part, and the Fibonacci-Lucas identity then contradicts Siegel finiteness on a nonsingular quartic.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2026 preprint obtains only one genus-theoretic factor of 2 in this Kishi family by forcing 5 and 3001 into the squarefree part. Searches for arbitrary 2-rank, powers-of-two class-number divisibility, and equivalent squarefree-kernel formulations in the same Fibonacci family found no prior coverage. Kishi's 2008 full text was not inspected and remains the principal residual source risk, although its abstract and its main results as reported in later work do not indicate the present theorem.

value.rationale: The result upgrades a recent divisibility-by-10 subfamily to infinite subfamilies with arbitrarily large 2-rank and class number divisible by 5*2^R, while preserving the specific Fibonacci-parametrized Kishi family and proving that the constructed fields are genuinely infinite and distinct.
